text_blocks.snippet: Type 2 diabetes is diagnosed using specific blood tests that measure your average or current blood sugar levels.
snippet_highlighted_words: using specific blood tests that measure your average or current blood sugar levels

text_blocks.snippet: Doctors use the guidelines from the American Diabetes Association to confirm a diagnosis:

list.snippet: A1C Test: Measures your average blood sugar over the past two to three months. A result of 6.5% or higher indicates diabetes.
Fasting Plasma Glucose (FPG) Test: Measures your blood sugar after you do not eat or drink anything except water for at least 8 hours. A result of 126 mg/dL (7.0 mmol/L) or higher indicates diabetes.
Oral Glucose Tolerance Test (OGTT): Measures your blood sugar two hours after you drink a special sugary liquid. A result of 200 mg/dL (11.1 mmol/L) or higher indicates diabetes.
Random Plasma Glucose Test: Measures your blood sugar at any time when you have classic symptoms of high blood sugar. A result of 200 mg/dL (11.1 mmol/L) or higher indicates diabetes.

text_blocks.snippet: If you do not have clear symptoms of high blood sugar, doctors usually require a repeat of the same test or a second different test from a blood sample to confirm the diagnosis. You can learn more about standard evaluations at the Mayo Clinic.
